 JUDGMENT

Since these two appeals arise from the very same award dated 07.08.2018 in O.P.(MV) No.275 of 2012 on the file of the additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Attingal, these appeals are heard together and being disposed of by this judgment.

M.A.C.A. No.2759 of 2019 is filed by the 2nd respondent/ insurer challenging the liability to pay the award amount whereas M.A.C.A.No.3744 of 2019 is filed by the claimant for enhancing compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
For brevity, the parties are referred to as they are arrayed before the tribunal.

2. According to the claimant, on 03.01.2012 at 6:00 p.m, while the claimant was travelling as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KL-16/H-1990, an autorickshaw bearing Reg.
No.KL-16/H-428 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner, knocked down the claimant, whereby he sustained serious injuries.
The claimant approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 10,75,000/- limited to 7,00,000/-.
3. The first respondent, owner-cum driver of the offending vehicle, remained ex parte before the tribunal.
The second MACA NOS. 2759 & 3744 OF 2019 2026:KER:10339 : 4 :
respondent/insurer filed a written statement admitting the policy but denying liability.
Before the tribunal, Exts.A1 to A8 were marked.

The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded an amount of 5,65,200/- with interest @9% per annum as compensation under different heads against the 2nd respondent being the insurer; and in default of payment as above, penal interest @
12% per annum was also awarded.
Challenging and dissatisfied with the impugned award, the insurer and the claimant have come up with the above appeals respectively.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the claimant and the learned standing counsel for the insurance company.
5. The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that there was negligence on the part of the claimant in causing the accident.

It is further submitted that in the statement given by the driver of the autorickshaw before the appellant insurance company it is stated that the claimant was the rider and he did not have any valid driving licence to ride the motorcycle.

On a perusal of the award, it is seen that though contention has been taken in the written statement, no evidence has been adduced by the insurance company to prove any contributory negligence on the part of the claimant herein.

sentences.text: 3 Accordingly, I am not inclined to accept the contention regarding negligence.

As regards the quantum of compensation, both sides challenged under the following heads: -
Notional income:-

The learned counsel for the claimant submitted that though an amount of 12,000/- was claimed as the income of the injured, who was a rubber tapper, the tribunal had taken only an amount of 5,000/- which is on the lower side.
No evidence is adduced to prove that the claimant was a rubber tapper.

The learned Counsel further submits that even going by the judgment in Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the income of a Coolie for an accident in 2012 is fixed at 8,500/- and sought for enhancement of the income.

entities.text:
Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to award a just and reasonable compensation and considering the principles laid down in Ramachandrappa (supra), I am inclined to re-fix the monthly income at 8,500/-.

Since the injured was a rubber tapper, who was aged 35 years at the time of the accident, following the judgment in National Insurance Co. Ltd v. Pranay Sethi & Ors [2017 (4) KLT 662 SC], 40% future prospects are to be added.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd v. Pranay Sethi & Ors [2017 (4) KLT 662 SC]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
By adding 40% future prospects, I find that the monthly income will be 11,900/- (8,500 + 40% of 8,500) for the purpose of awarding MACA NOS. 2759 & 3744 OF 2019 2026:KER:10339 : 6 :
compensation towards permanent disability.
Loss of earnings:- The learned counsel for the claimant submitted that for awarding compensation under the head loss of earnings, the tribunal has taken only a period of six months.

The claimant sustained the following injury:-
(1) Type III compound comminuted fracture of both bones of right leg.
Considering the injuries sustained, I find that a period of eight months is reasonable for awarding compensation under the head loss of earnings.
Since the notional income is fixed as 8,500, I find that a total amount of 68,000/- (8,500 x 8) is payable under the afore head.
Since the tribunal has awarded only an amount of 30,000/- under the afore head, there will be an additional amount of 38,000/- under the head loss of earnings.
Loss of amenities :
- On a perusal of the award, it is seen that the Tribunal though an amount of 3,00,000/- was claimed, the tribunal had awarded only an amount of 50,000/- towards loss of amenities.
Considering the injuries sustained by the claimant and the loss of enjoyment in life, I deem it appropriate to award a total compensation of 1,50,000/- towards loss of amenities.

Since the tribunal has awarded only an amount of 50,000/- under the afore head, there will be an additional amount of 1,00,000/-
MACA NOS. 2759 & 3744 OF 2019 2026:KER:10339 : 7 :
under the head loss of amenities.

sentences.text: Pain and suffering:-

The learned counsel for the claimant submits that though an amount of 2,00,000/- was claimed, the tribunal had awarded only an amount of 75,000/- towards pain and suffering, which is on the lower side.
Considering the injuries sustained by the claimant, I am inclined to grant an amount of 1,50,000/- to the claimant as a total compensation towards pain and suffering.
Since the tribunal has awarded an amount of 75,000/- under the afore head, there will be an additional amount of 75,000/- under the head pain and suffering.
Permanent disability:-
The learned counsel for the claimant submitted that though in Ext.A8 disability, the percentage of disability was shown as 75%, the tribunal originally had reduced the percentage of disability to 8%.
Thereafter, the review petition was filed and the percentage of disability was modified to 30%.
There was an amputation of the right leg below the knee
However,
on verifying the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923, the percentage of loss of earning capacity for amputation of leg below the knee is fixed as 50%.
Hence, I am inclined to refix the percentage of disability as 50%, by following the loss of earning capacity fixed in the afore Act.

Since the monthly income after MACA NOS. 2759 & 3744 OF 2019 2026:KER:10339 : 8 :
adding 40% future prospects is fixed at 11,900/-, following the judgments in Pranay Sethi (supra) and Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010(2) KLT 802(SC)], the percentage of disability is recalculated as: 11,42,400/- (11,900 x 12 x 16 x 50%).

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010(2) KLT 802(SC)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since, the tribunal has awarded an amount of 4,03,200/- under the head permanent disability, there will be an additional amount of 7,39,200/- under the afore head.
Purchase of Prosthesis :- On a perusal of the award, it is seen that the tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards purchase of prosthesis.
Admittedly, there was amputation of the right leg below the knee and considering the age of the claimant at the time of the accident as 35 years.
I find it appropriate to award an amount of 5,00,000/- towards purchase of prosthesis.
For want of documents to show whether any prosthesis was purchased, I find it appropriate to grant interest for the afore 5,00,000/- from the date of this judgment till realisation.

6. Though the claimant claimed enhancement of compensation under the other heads, on a perusal of the records available, I am not inclined to interfere with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads since it appears to be just and reasonable.

Since the appeal is of the year 2019, I find it MACA NOS. 2759 & 3744 OF 2019 2026:KER:10339 : 9 :
reasonable to fix the interest @ 8% per annum on the enhanced amount.
7.

On a perusal of the impugned award, it is seen that the tribunal awarded penal interest at the rate of 12%, which is not legally sustainable in view of the judgment of the apex court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Keshav Bahadur [2004 (2) SCC 370].

sentences.text: Accordingly, the direction of the tribunal awarding penal interest @ 12% per annum is hereby set aside.

The amount of 5,00,000/- awarded towards purchase of Prosthesis, will carry interest from the date of this judgment till realization.
The respondent insurer shall deposit the said amount together with interest and costs within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
The direction of the tribunal awarding penal interest @ 12% per annum is hereby set aside.

The appellant/ claimant shall furnish copies of the PAN Card, AADHAAR Card and bank details before the MACA NOS. 2759 & 3744 OF 2019 2026:KER:10339 : 11 :
respondent insurer within a period of one month so as to enable the insurance company to make the deposit as ordered above.
In case of failure to furnish details as above, it shall be open for the insurance company to deposit the said amount before the tribunal.
Upon such deposit being made, the entire amount shall be disbursed to the appellant/ claimant at the earliest in accordance with law.
However, it is made clear that the enhanced compensation will not carry interest for the period of delay of 287 days in filing the appeal.
